One has only to suppose an initial accentuation in Illyrian: Dyrrachium, Isamnus, Drivastum (cf. Messapian Brundisium > Brindisi). [fn. 361: Cf. Çabej (1958: 59).] || Krahe 1943: 34: „ähnlich das Keltische und vielleicht auch das Illyrische haben eine Anfangsbetonung (Initialakzent) durchgeführt, d. h. sie haben den freien Wortakzent des Idg. auf die erste Silbe eines jeden Wortes festgelegt.“
new_statements.translation: Krahe 1943: 34: 'similarly Celtic and perhaps also Illyrian carried through an initial accent (Initialakzent), i.e. they fixed the free Indo-European word accent on the first syllable of every word.' Neroznak 1978: 161: 'in Illyrian and Messapic and, apparently, in Proto-Albanian the accent was proparoxytonic; through the loss of the final syllable, paroxytone accent is established in Albanian: Dyrrachium – Alb. Durrës / Messapic Brundisium (mod. Brindisi).'

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent is supposed to have been fixed on the first syllable of the word (Krahe: the free PIE accent was fixed on the first syllable of every word; Katičić: initial accentuation, inferred from toponyms; Neroznak: proparoxytone on the same toponyms). No direct evidence exists; the claim is a hypothesis used to explain Albanian/Italian reflexes and medial syncope in names.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Neroznak 1978: 161 frames the same evidence as 'proparoxytone' (antepenultimate) rather than initial; for the trisyllabic examples the two coincide.
new_statements.domain_note: Reconstructive inference, not observation: Illyrian left no texts and its names are transmitted in Greek/Latin spelling without accent marks. All three statements infer word-level initial accent from (a) the initial stress of Albanian and Italian reflexes of ancient toponyms (Dyrrachium > Durrës, Isamnus > Ishëm, Drivastum > Drisht, Polatum > Pult; Messapic Brundisium > Bríndisi) and (b) syncope of medial syllables in names (Krahe: ven. zants vs illyr. Zanatis). Domain is the word (proper names); nothing on citation forms or phrase accent.
new_statements.identity_note: Illyrian (illy1234) is an extinct language known only from onomastics and glosses in Greek and Latin sources; no text shows accent. The statements found concern 'Illyrian' in the narrow Balkan sense (southern Illyrian of the Albanian coast, toponyms Dyrrachium/Isamnus/Drivastum/Polatum) and are argued jointly with Messapic (mess1244: Brundisium > Bríndisi) and Proto-Albanian (alba1267). The earlier mess1244 check quoted the same Katičić passage and correctly assigned its scope to Illyrian. Because the accent is a reconstructive hypothesis (toponym reflexes + name syncope), any catalog entry should be flagged 'inferred, extinct, no direct evidence' with confidence low.

new_statements.quote: 1962 item scanned snippet (verbatim, incl. scanned errors): "vielleicht auch das Illyrische haben eine Anfangsbetonung (Initialakzent) durchgefiihrt, d. h. sie" and "Germ, auf Grand der stark dynamischen Anfangsbetonung (vgl. § 13) mannigfache Scliwa- chungen". Full sentence as printed in the 1943 ed. p. 34: "Einige Sprachen, so das spätere Urgermanische ... und das „Uritalische“ (d. h. die Vorstufen des Lateinischen und Oskisch-Umbrischen, vgl. § 2,11), ähnlich das Keltische und vielleicht auch das Illyrische haben eine Anfangsbetonung (Initialakzent) durchgeführt, d. h. sie haben den freien Wortakzent des Idg. auf die erste Silbe eines jeden Wortes festgelegt."
new_statements.translation: Some languages, such as later Proto-Germanic ... and 'Proto-Italic' (i.e. the prestages of Latin and Osco-Umbrian), likewise Celtic and perhaps also Illyrian, carried through an initial accentuation (initial accent), i.e. they fixed the free Indo-European word accent on the first syllable of every word.
new_statements.citation: Krahe, Hans. 1962/1966. Indogermanische Sprachwissenschaft, I: Einleitung und Lautlehre (Sammlung Göschen 59), 4th/5th ed. Berlin: de Gruyter. §10.
new_statements.locator: 1962 ed.: II. Teil Lautlehre, A. Die Betonung, §13 (Germanic passage cross-refers 'vgl. § 13'; §11 'Funktion und Arten des Akzents' begins p. 49 per the TOC snippet; page of the Illyrian sentence not visible in the snippet). Same sentence in the 1943 ed. §10 'Der Wortakzent', p. 34 (page marker 34 precedes, 35 follows in the djvu text).
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Both quoted snippets are present verbatim (scanned errors included) in (highlight.text: 'vielleicht auch das Illyrische haben eine Anfangsbetonung (Initialakzent) durchgefiihrt, d. h. sie' and 'Germ, auf Grand der stark dynamischen Anfangsbetonung (vgl. § 13) mannigfache Scliwa- chungen'; filename.gz, meta_date 1962). The full 1943 sentence is at lines 1842-1849, between page marker '34' (line 1809, followed by the running head 'Lautlehre') and '35', inside §10 (§11 'Der Silbenakzent' begins right after): 'Einige Sprachen, so das spätere Urgermanische.. und das "Uritalische".., ähnlich das Keltische und vielleicht auch das Illyrische haben eine Anfangsbetonung (Initialakzent) durchgeführt,…
new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (fixed initial pattern) and the existing Katičić 1976: 186 statement of initial accentuation; adds the hedge 'perhaps' and the explicit framing that the free PIE accent was fixed on the first syllable of every word. The 1962 item is lending-only on archive.org (access-restricted; and pdf both not reachable by automated download), so the wording was confirmed through archive.org's full-text-search snippet of that item's scanned and the identical sentence in the open 1943 edition already held by the project.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Illyrian is listed (with the hedge 'vielleicht', perhaps) among the IE languages that replaced the free PIE word accent with a fixed accent on the first syllable of every word.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the claim is hedged ('vielleicht auch das Illyrische') and, as Illyrian is unwritten, rests on inference (syncope in names such as Venetic zants ~ Illyrian Zanatis per Mayer 1939: 109, and Albanian/Italian reflexes of ancient toponyms per Katičić 1976: 186).
new_statements.identity_note: Krahe writes of 'das Illyrische' in the broad mid-20th-century sense (the language of the ancient Illyrians of the western Balkans, at that time also taken to include Venetic-type and Pannonian names); the inference for initial accent comes from name syncope (Zanatis ~ zants) and Albanian reflexes of toponyms (Dyrrachium > Durrës, Drivastum > Drisht), i.e. from the Albania/Dalmatia onomastic corpus, not from any dialect description.

new_statements.quote: 1943 ed. p. 34 (§10): "Einige Sprachen, so das spätere Urgermanische (d. h. nach jener Periode, in welcher die zuvor geschilderte Spirantenerweichung eintrat) und das „Uritalische“ (d. h. die Vorstufen des Lateinischen und Oskisch-Umbrischen, vgl. § 2,11), ähnlich das Keltische und vielleicht auch das Illyrische haben eine Anfangsbetonung (Initialakzent) durchgeführt, d. h. sie haben den freien Wortakzent des Idg. auf die erste Silbe eines jeden Wortes festgelegt." 1962 ed. scanned snippet (archive.org FTS, verbatim incl. scanned errors): "des Keltischen und vielleicht auch das Illyrische haben eine Anfangsbetonung (Initialakzent) durchgefiihrt, d. h. sie".
new_statements.translation: Some languages, thus later Proto-Germanic (i.e. after the period in which the spirant weakening described above took place) and 'Proto-Italic' (i.e. the pre-stages of Latin and Osco-Umbrian, cf. §2,11), similarly Celtic and perhaps also Illyrian, carried through an initial accentuation (initial accent), i.e. they fixed the free word accent of Indo-European on the first syllable of every word.
new_statements.citation: Krahe, Hans. 1962/1966. Indogermanische Sprachwissenschaft, I: Einleitung und Lautlehre (Sammlung Göschen 59), 4th/5th ed. Berlin: de Gruyter. §10.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement (initial) as the catalog record (Katičić 1976: 186 'initial accentuation in Illyrian', after Çabej 1958: 59) and as the two existing statements (Katičić 1976; Krahe 1962/1943). Adds nothing beyond what is held by the project except the edition mapping (§10 of 1943 = §13 of 1962/66) and the list of gated digital copies of the later editions.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Krahe reconstructs, with the hedge 'vielleicht' (perhaps), that Illyrian, like Proto-Germanic, Proto-Italic and Celtic, gave up the free Indo-European word accent and fixed the accent on the first syllable of every word (Initialakzent). This is a comparative inference for a fragmentarily attested language (names and glosses), not an observed rule.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the whole statement is hedged ('vielleicht auch das Illyrische')
new_statements.identity_note: Krahe's 'das Illyrische' is the ancient Indo-European language of the western Balkans (his §2 list, item 13/10: 'Das Illyrische, das einst weite Strecken Europas..', written in his pan-Illyrian period, so his 'Illyrian' is geographically broader than the modern restriction to south Dalmatia/Albania noted by Duridanov 2002); Messapic is treated separately. The accent statement concerns reconstructed Illyrian word accent inferred from syncope in names, not an observed variety.
